# Preface {.unnumbered}

Every processor, controller, and screen you have ever used began as a
handful of logic gates someone arranged on purpose. This book is about
learning to do that arranging yourself — not by reading about it, but by
designing, simulating, and running your own digital circuits on real
hardware.

Over nine labs, you will go from your first combinational circuit to a
complete FPGA-based System on Chip: a HIPV, a Risc-V based processor, talking to
peripherals you wrote, over a bus you configured, validated with a real
oscilloscope. Along the way you will hit the same problems every digital
designer hits — a signal that glitches, a counter that free-runs, a
testbench that lies to you — and learn to reason your way out of them.

That debugging instinct, more than any single lab, is the point.

**Note to Students**: These notes are intended solely for educational
purposes. They are not a replacement for attending lectures or consulting
textbooks, but rather a complementary resource to support your learning.
